主要内容: The U.S. Department of the Treasury and the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) announced the first round of Opportunity Zones designations for 18 states on April 9, 2018. The Tax Cuts and Jobs Act created Opportunity Zones to encourage investment in distressed communities. These zones offer preferential tax treatment for new investments. States, D.C., and U.S. possessions were required to submit nominations by March 21st, with Treasury having 30 days to designate the zones. The designated states include American Samoa, Arizona, California, Colorado, Georgia, Idaho, Kentucky, Michigan, Mississippi, Nebraska, New Jersey, Oklahoma, Puerto Rico, South Carolina, South Dakota, Vermont, Virgin Islands, and Wisconsin. Qualified Opportunity Zones retain their designation for 10 years, and investors can defer taxes until December 31, 2026, if the gains are reinvested in a Qualified Opportunity Fund. The Treasury and IRS plan to issue additional guidance on Qualified Opportunity Funds, including certification requirements.
